programs.target: DMD exon 55 skipping — intended for patients whose deletion is made in-frame by removing exon 55 alone, NOT an exon-55 nonsense lesion
programs.delivery: Antigen-binding fragment (Fab) against transferrin receptor 1 conjugated to a PMO; same Fab, linker and payload chemistry as z-rostudirsen (DYNE-251), IV
programs.stage: Preclinical, advancing into IND-enabling studies; in vitro exon-skipping data only, presented 27th Annual NMSG Scientific Meeting, San Antonio, 25–27 Sep 2026 (no skipping % or dystrophin % disclosed)
programs.key_result: An exon-55-directed PMO sequence with a muscle-targeting delivery vehicle now exists at IND-enabling stage, alongside DYNE-253 (ex53), DYNE-245 (ex45), DYNE-244 (ex44). Only in vivo PK/PD disclosed in the set was for DYNE-253 in a Del52 mouse; nothing in vivo for DYNE-255.
programs.changes_decision_because: Supplies half of a 54+55 or 55+56 cocktail; makes exon-55 ASO a licensing/IP question, not a discovery one.

programs.program: z-rostudirsen / zeleciment rostudirsen (DYNE-251), DELIVER trial registrational expansion cohort
programs.target: DMD exon 51 skipping (different splice target — chemistry, dosing, delivery and regulatory precedent only, not a potency expectation for exon 55)
programs.delivery: TfR1-Fab–PMO conjugate, IV once every 4 weeks
programs.stage: BLA accepted with Priority Review; PDUFA target action date 21 Jan 2027; accelerated approval on dystrophin surrogate; potential US launch Q1 2027
programs.key_result: Registrational expansion cohort (n=32, ambulatory and non-ambulatory): muscle-content-adjusted dystrophin 5.46% of normal at 6 months, met primary endpoint, functional improvement across multiple endpoints through 18 months in earlier cohorts, favourable safety; FDA confirmed dystrophin-as-surrogate accelerated approval remains available.
programs.changes_decision_because: De-risks TfR1-Fab–PMO delivery to DMD muscle and fixes the regulatory and dosing template.

programs.organization: Avidity Biosciences / Novartis (acquisition expected to close H1 2026)
programs.program: del-zota / delpacibart zotadirsen (AOC 1044); EXPLORE44, EXPLORE44-OLE, Phase 3 SAFARI44 (NCT07587242)
programs.target: DMD exon 44 skipping (adjacent-region, different exon; precedent only)
programs.delivery: Antibody-oligonucleotide conjugate — anti-TfR1 mAb + PMO, IV every 6 weeks
programs.stage: BLA accepted for substantive review, Priority Review, accelerated approval pathway; Breakthrough Therapy; US Managed Access Program open; Phase 3 SAFARI44 recruiting as confirmatory
programs.key_result: At 5 mg/kg q6w x3 doses: exon 44 skipping +37% (7%→44%), dystrophin 7%→32% of normal, CK reduced >80% toward normal, favourable safety; 1-year EXPLORE44/OLE showed sustained CK reduction and functional improvement. Preclinical AOC in humanised del45 mice restored dystrophin to ~10% WT in gastrocnemius and ~5% in heart after a single IV dose.
programs.changes_decision_because: Sets the efficacy bar and shows TfR1 conjugates reach heart; Novartis now owns the leading platform, narrowing partner options.

programs.program: PGN-EDO51 (CONNECT1-EDO51 NCT06079736 terminated; CONNECT2-EDO51 NCT06833931 withdrawn) — DISCONTINUED May 2025, all DMD R&D wound down
programs.delivery: EDO peptide (cell-penetrating Enhanced Delivery Oligonucleotide) conjugated PMO, IV
programs.key_result: At 10 mg/kg, exon-51-skipped transcript reached only 4.26% and total dystrophin only 0.59% of normal — failed internal dystrophin target despite measurable skipping. Both DMD trials stopped (one never dosed).
programs.changes_decision_because: Proves skipped-transcript % does not predict dystrophin; a two-exon skip must be powered on protein, not RT-PCR.

programs.organization: Nippon Shinyaku / National Center of Neurology and Psychiatry (NCNP), Japan
programs.program: Brogidirsen (NS-089/NCNP-02); Phase 1/2 plus ongoing global Phase 2 (NCT05996003)
programs.target: DMD exon 44 skipping via a DUAL-targeting design — two oligonucleotides directed at the same exon, developed as one product
programs.stage: 5-year efficacy/safety data presented at World Muscle Society Congress, Hiroshima, 29 Sep – 3 Oct 2026; FDA Breakthrough Therapy; global Phase 2 ongoing
programs.key_result: Through 5 years: NSAA improved or maintained in participants remaining ambulant; upper-limb function maintained in all, including those who became non-ambulant; no serious or severe brogidirsen-related AEs, no infusion reactions, no discontinuations.
programs.changes_decision_because: Only clinical precedent that a multi-oligonucleotide single product is developable and regulable — the 54+55 cocktail's key risk.

programs.target: DMD exon 53 skipping (different target; chemistry/dosing precedent only)
programs.delivery: Unconjugated stereopure PN (phosphoryl guanidine) backbone oligonucleotide, IV monthly
programs.stage: Phase 2 complete through 48 weeks; NDA for accelerated approval intended in 2026; FDA confirmed dystrophin surrogate pathway open
programs.key_result: 48 weeks: mean dystrophin 7.8% of normal with 88% of boys above 5%, stable between 24 and 48 weeks; 61-day muscle tissue half-life supporting monthly dosing; functional benefit and reversal of muscle-damage markers; no SAEs, no discontinuations.
programs.changes_decision_because: Shows a non-conjugate backbone can hit ~8% dystrophin — a credible fallback if conjugate access is blocked.

programs.program: BMN 351 / nivudirsen; Phase 1/2 NCT06280209 and OLE NCT07573631
programs.target: DMD exon 51 skipping (different target; benchmark only)
programs.delivery: Unconjugated antisense oligonucleotide, IV dose escalation (6–9 mg/kg)
programs.stage: Phase 1/2 active, not recruiting; OLE enrolling by invitation; interim data at MDA 2026; confirmatory studies planned
programs.key_result: Week 25 dystrophin change from baseline: 4.50% (±4.71) by western blot and 4.76% (±4.45) by LC-MS at 9 mg/kg (vs ~1.3–1.9% at 6 mg/kg); acceptable safety at ≤9 mg/kg; PK/PD modelling predicts further rise toward steady state.
programs.changes_decision_because: Second unconjugated benchmark near 5%; sets the minimum a two-oligo cocktail must beat to justify its complexity.

programs.program: AMONDYS 45 / VYONDYS 53 accelerated-to-traditional approval sNDAs; ELEVIDYS ENDEAVOR Cohort 8; corporate restructuring toward siRNA
programs.target: DMD exons 45 and 53 skipping (marketed naked PMOs) plus AAV microdystrophin
programs.delivery: Unconjugated PMO, IV weekly; AAVrh74 for ELEVIDYS
programs.stage: sNDAs accepted for review (ESSENCE confirmatory data + real-world evidence); ELEVIDYS distribution halted by FDA after patient deaths, Cohort 8 with sirolimus pretreatment enrolling to year-end 2026; 36% workforce cut (~500 roles, ~$400M/yr) and pipeline reprioritised to siRNA assets (SRP-1001 FSHD1, SRP-1003 DM1)
programs.key_result: The naked-PMO incumbents are being pushed to confirm clinical benefit while their originator exits DMD oligonucleotide discovery in favour of siRNA; AAV gene therapy for DMD has a live safety crisis.
programs.changes_decision_because: Frees competitive space for a conjugated double-skip, but raises the confirmatory-benefit bar and devalues AAV comparators.

programs.organization: Entrada Therapeutics (DMD franchise wholly owned; Vertex partnership is DM1/VX-670 only)
programs.target: DMD exons 44, 45, 50, 51 skipping (franchise approach across the hotspot; exon 50 is immediately adjacent to the enumerated 50-55 and 50-57 blocks)
programs.delivery: Endosomal Escape Vehicle (EEV) peptide-conjugated PMO, IV
programs.stage: ENTR-601-44 Phase 1/2 Cohort 1 topline positive, OLE and Cohort 2 data expected by year-end 2026; ENTR-601-45 Phase 1/2 MAD dosing initiated; ENTR-601-50 MHRA authorisation granted, EU filings H2 2026 and study start by end-2026; ENTR-601-51 global filings in 2026
programs.key_result: ENTR-601-44 Cohort 1 showed statistically significant improvement in Time to Rise velocity in the majority of treated participants; Rare Pediatric Disease Designation granted. A peptide-conjugate DMD franchise is still advancing despite PepGen's peptide-conjugate failure.
programs.changes_decision_because: Keeps peptide-conjugate delivery live as an alternative to TfR1, and an exon-50 ASO enters the neighbourhood.

programs.organization: PTC Therapeutics (regulatory action by European Commission / EMA CHMP)
programs.program: Translarna (ataluren) — conditional EU marketing authorisation NOT renewed, 28 March 2025; remains available in the UK
programs.target: Nonsense-mutation DMD specifically — the same patient class as this exon-55 PTC lesion, via small-molecule readthrough (not an ASO mechanism)
programs.stage: EU authorisation withdrawn; three RCTs (007, 020, 041) failed their primary 6MWD endpoints
programs.key_result: CHMP concluded effectiveness was not confirmed after repeated 2024 re-examinations; EC confirmed non-renewal. Nonsense-mutation DMD patients in the EU now have no mutation-specific approved therapy.
programs.changes_decision_because: Removes the incumbent comparator for exon-55 nonsense patients and defines a clean unmet need.

programs.organization: Precision BioSciences (PBGENE-DMD) and academic single-AAV base-editing groups
programs.program: FUNCTION-DMD first-in-human gene editing (patient dosed); single-vector adenine base editing of a DMD nonsense variant (MDA 2026); dual-AAV9 base editor for exon 50 skipping (NCT06392724, Peking Union Medical College Hospital)
programs.target: Permanent DNA-level correction, including nonsense variants specifically (e.g. DMD c.9445C>T p.Q3149X) — the direct competitor mechanism for a point-mutation lesion
programs.stage: PBGENE-DMD first patient dosed, US sites activating; base editing of nonsense variants at humanised-mouse / patient-myoblast stage (MDA 2026 abstract); dual-AAV9 exon-50 base editor in a Phase 1-type trial in children 4–10
programs.key_result: Up to 88.2±1.7% correction of a DMD nonsense mutation in patient-derived primary myoblasts ex vivo; single IV dose gave ~85% dystrophin rescue in heart and 20–40% across skeletal muscles in mouse models — one-time full-length restoration rather than internally deleted Becker protein.
programs.changes_decision_because: Nonsense-specific editing targets exactly this lesion with full-length protein, so an ASO must win on chronic safety and speed.

programs.organization: Academic (Disease Models & Mechanisms, 29 Sep 2025, DOI 10.1242/dmm.050595) — not a commercial program
programs.program: CRISPR-generated Dmd Δ52-55 Becker mouse model
programs.target: Functional validation of exactly the enumerated in-frame block 52-55 (-225 aa, aa 2515-2739) that contains exon 55
programs.delivery: Not applicable — genetic model, no delivery agent
programs.key_result: At 12 weeks: WT-like levels of truncated dystrophin with normal DGC localisation (alpha-syntrophin, beta-sarcoglycan) at the sarcolemma, <1% centralised nuclei, normal grip strength and tetanic force, protection from exercise-induced damage; cardiac anatomy and ejection fraction WT-like through 52 weeks. At 52 weeks after exercise: reduced forelimb grip strength and contractile force vs WT, with Hspa1a/Hspa1b up 97- and 50-fold. Authors conclude the truncated protein is sufficient when young but insufficient to maintain homeostasis and resist exercise damage with age.
programs.changes_decision_because: The rod-deleting block containing exon 55 makes sarcolemma-anchoring dystrophin, but large deletions degrade with age — favour the minimal 54-55 or 55-56 skip.

programs.organization: Academic / clinical genetics groups (2025 case report, PMC12043877) — not a commercial program
programs.program: Incidental DMD exons 48-55 deletion identified in prenatal diagnosis (SNP-array, confirmed by MLPA and long-read sequencing)
programs.target: Human genotype-phenotype evidence for the enumerated in-frame block 48-55 (-435 aa, aa 2305-2739)
programs.key_result: First reported prenatal DMD exons 48-55 deletion; the male carrier was asymptomatic with normal serum biochemical indicators. Authors caution that DMD phenotypes are diverse and severity should not be predicted from molecular findings alone. Related literature reports normal phenotypes in fathers carrying predicted in-frame central-rod-domain DMD CNVs detected as NIPT secondary findings.
programs.changes_decision_because: Human evidence that even a large in-frame rod deletion spanning exon 55 can be near-asymptomatic, validating large-skip fallbacks.

programs.organization: Academic PMO-cocktail groups (NCNP/Japan, Leiden, and collaborators) — no clinical program found
programs.program: Mutation-tailored exon 45-55 multi-exon skipping PMO cocktails (Mol Ther 2019, PMID 31416775; PLoS ONE 2018 PMC5957359; mdx52 in vivo PMID 30171548; PNAS bodywide 45-55)
programs.target: Coordinated multi-exon skipping across 45-55, which includes exon 55 and every enumerated larger in-frame block (50-55, 52-55, 52-57, 53-58, 54-57, 54-59, 48-55 and others)
programs.delivery: Unconjugated PMO cocktails, local and systemic in mice; in vitro in patient-derived and immortalised DMD cells
programs.stage: Preclinical only — I found no 2025-2026 clinical or IND-stage multi-exon cocktail program
programs.key_result: Cocktails skipped up to 10 exons in immortalised DMD muscle cells with dystrophin restoration; simultaneous skipping of all 11 exons 45-55 demonstrated in humanised mice carrying the normal human DMD gene; substantive 45-55 skipping achieved in myotubes transdifferentiated from DMD patient fibroblasts; bodywide 45-55 skipping shown in mdx52 mice. A companion PMO-library study shows skipping efficiency correlates with flanking intron retention time and is significantly higher when the ASO targets the proximal (5') region of the exon.
programs.changes_decision_because: Coordinated multi-exon skipping is real but only preclinical; the intron-timing and 5'-targeting rules should drive our 54/55/56 ASO walk.

as_of: 2026-10-08 (most recent disclosures retrieved: Dyne DYNE-255 preclinical presentation at NMSG, 25–27 Sep 2026; brogidirsen 5-year data at World Muscle Society, Hiroshima, 29 Sep – 3 Oct 2026)
